source: import java.util.*; class ReachA { int count(Map<Integer,List<Integer>> g,int root){ Set<Integer>s=new HashSet<>(); ArrayDeque<Integer>q=new ArrayDeque<>(); s.add(root);q.add(root);int n=0;while(!q.isEmpty()){int u=q.removeFirst();n++;for(int v:g.get(u))if(s.add(v))q.addLast(v);}return n;} }

mathematical_rationale: Each reachable vertex is queued and expanded once; every stored neighbor entry is scanned once.
assumptions: Expected O(1) HashSet and ArrayDeque operations.
E is the total adjacency-entry count.

source: import java.util.*; class ReachB { Set<Integer> walk(HashMap<Integer,List<Integer>>g,List<Integer>starts){Set<Integer>seen=new HashSet<>();Deque<Integer>q=new ArrayDeque<>();for(int s:starts)if(seen.add(s))q.offer(s);while(!q.isEmpty()){int u=q.poll();for(int v:g.get(u))if(seen.add(v))q.offer(v);}return seen;} }

source: import java.util.*; class ReachC { int all(Map<Integer,List<Integer>>g){Set<Integer>seen=new HashSet<>();int n=0;for(int seed:g.keySet()){if(seen.add(seed)){Deque<Integer>q=new ArrayDeque<>();q.add(seed);while(!q.isEmpty()){int u=q.remove();n++;for(int v:g.getOrDefault(u,List.of()))if(seen.add(v))q.add(v);}}}return n;} }

source: import java.util.*; class ReachD { int walk(List<Integer>[]a,int s){boolean[]seen=new boolean[a.length];Queue<Integer>q=new ArrayDeque<>();seen[s]=true;q.add(s);while(!q.isEmpty()){int u=q.remove();for(int v:a[u])if(!seen[v]){seen[v]=true;q.add(v);}}return 0;} }

source: import java.util.*; class MatrixWalk { int run(boolean[][]m,int s){int n=m.length;boolean[]seen=new boolean[n];Queue<Integer>q=new ArrayDeque<>();seen[s]=true;q.add(s);while(!q.isEmpty()){int u=q.remove();for(int v=0;v<n;v++)if(m[u][v]&&!seen[v]){seen[v]=true;q.add(v);}}return 0;} }
input_constraints_and_representation: V by V boolean matrix; each dequeued node scans every column.
mathematical_rationale: At most V vertices are dequeued, each with a V-entry row scan.
assumptions: Matrix, visited and queue operations are O(1).

source: import java.util.*; class QueryWalk { int all(Map<Integer,List<Integer>>g,int[]starts){int total=0;for(int s:starts){Set<Integer>seen=new HashSet<>();Queue<Integer>q=new ArrayDeque<>();seen.add(s);q.add(s);while(!q.isEmpty()){int u=q.remove();total++;for(int v:g.getOrDefault(u,List.of()))if(seen.add(v))q.add(v);}}return total;} }

source: import java.util.*; class OrderedWalk { int run(TreeMap<Integer,List<Integer>>g,int s){TreeSet<Integer>seen=new TreeSet<>();Queue<Integer>q=new ArrayDeque<>();seen.add(s);q.add(s);while(!q.isEmpty()){int u=q.remove();for(int v:g.getOrDefault(u,List.of()))if(seen.add(v))q.add(v);}return seen.size();} }

mathematical_rationale: Ordered lookup and membership/insertion cost O(log V); scanning E entries gives O(E log V), plus vertex work.
assumptions: Tree operations are worst-case O(log V).

source: import java.util.*; class EdgeWalk { static class E{int a,b;E(int x,int y){a=x;b=y;}} int run(List<E>edges,int n,int s){boolean[]seen=new boolean[n];Queue<Integer>q=new ArrayDeque<>();seen[s]=true;q.add(s);while(!q.isEmpty()){int u=q.remove();for(E e:edges){int v=e.a==u?e.b:(e.b==u?e.a:-1);if(v>=0&&!seen[v]){seen[v]=true;q.add(v);}}}return 0;} }
input_constraints_and_representation: Edges stored once in a flat list; every dequeued vertex scans all E records.
mathematical_rationale: There are at most V dequeues and each scans E edges.
assumptions: Visited and queue operations are O(1).

source: import java.util.*; class NestedWork { int run(List<List<Integer>>g,int n,int s){Set<Integer>seen=new HashSet<>();Queue<Integer>q=new ArrayDeque<>();seen.add(s);q.add(s);while(!q.isEmpty()){int u=q.remove();for(int i=0;i<n;i++)consume(i);for(int v:g.get(u))if(seen.add(v))q.add(v);}return 0;} void consume(int x){} }
input_constraints_and_representation: One full V-sized loop runs for each dequeued vertex, in addition to adjacency scanning.
mathematical_rationale: The repeated loop costs V*V; edge enumeration adds E.
assumptions: The extra loop always scans all V vertices.

source: import java.util.*; class TreeWalk { int run(List<List<Integer>>children,int root){Queue<Integer>q=new ArrayDeque<>();q.add(root);int n=0;while(!q.isEmpty()){int u=q.remove();n++;for(int v:children.get(u))q.add(v);}return n;} }

source: import java.util.*; class GridFour { int run(int[][]a,int sr,int sc){int r=a.length,c=a[0].length;boolean[][]seen=new boolean[r][c];int[]dr={1,-1,0,0},dc={0,0,1,-1};ArrayDeque<int[]>q=new ArrayDeque<>();seen[sr][sc]=true;q.add(new int[]{sr,sc});while(!q.isEmpty()){int[]p=q.remove();for(int d=0;d<4;d++){int x=p[0]+dr[d],y=p[1]+dc[d];if(x>=0&&x<r&&y>=0&&y<c&&a[x][y]==1&&!seen[x][y]){seen[x][y]=true;q.add(new int[]{x,y});}}}return 0;} }

mathematical_rationale: Each reachable cell enters once and checks four constant directions.
assumptions: R and C are dimensions; four is constant.

source: import java.util.*; class GridEight { int run(int[][]a,int sr,int sc){int r=a.length,c=a[0].length;boolean[][]seen=new boolean[r][c];int[]dr={-1,-1,-1,0,0,1,1,1},dc={-1,0,1,-1,1,-1,0,1};Deque<int[]>q=new ArrayDeque<>();seen[sr][sc]=true;q.addLast(new int[]{sr,sc});while(!q.isEmpty()){int[]p=q.removeFirst();for(int d=0;d<8;d++){int x=p[0]+dr[d],y=p[1]+dc[d];if(x>=0&&x<r&&y>=0&&y<c&&a[x][y]!=0&&!seen[x][y]){seen[x][y]=true;q.addLast(new int[]{x,y});}}}return 0;} }

source: import java.util.*; class GridScan { int run(int[][]a,int sr,int sc){int r=a.length,c=a[0].length;boolean[][]seen=new boolean[r][c];int[]dr={1,0,-1,0},dc={0,1,0,-1};Queue<int[]>q=new ArrayDeque<>();seen[sr][sc]=true;q.add(new int[]{sr,sc});while(!q.isEmpty()){int[]p=q.remove();for(int d=0;d<4;d++){int x=p[0]+dr[d],y=p[1]+dc[d];if(x>=0&&x<r&&y>=0&&y<c){for(int i=0;i<r;i++)for(int j=0;j<c;j++)inspect(a[i][j]);if(!seen[x][y]){seen[x][y]=true;q.add(new int[]{x,y});}}}}return 0;} void inspect(int x){} }
input_constraints_and_representation: Binary grid and each valid local neighbor candidate triggers a full grid scan before enqueueing.
mathematical_rationale: Each reachable cell has at most four candidates; in an all-open grid, each candidate incurs R*C scan work, giving O((R*C)^2) total.
assumptions: Grid cells are binary/nonnegative so the scan has no early-return exit.
Four candidates per cell is constant; R and C are dimensions.

source: import java.util.*; class IndexedWalk { int run(List<List<Integer>>g,int start){boolean[]seen=new boolean[g.size()];ArrayList<Integer>q=new ArrayList<>();q.add(start);seen[start]=true;for(int head=0;head<q.size();head++){int u=q.get(head);for(int v:g.get(u))if(!seen[v]){seen[v]=true;q.add(v);}}return q.size();} }

from collections import deque
def jobs(items):
    pending = deque(items)
    done = 0
    while pending:
        pending.popleft()
        done += 1
    return done
input_constraints_and_representation: A queue drains independent jobs; there is no graph or neighbor relation.
mathematical_rationale: Every item is removed once with constant work.
assumptions: This is a queue-only non-BFS control case.
